perf.summary: Horizon construction is O(F^2) per iteration via per-edge linear face scans; replace with an edge-counting / adjacency pass to make it O(F) (or O(F*E)).
perf.currentCost: For each visible face, IsHorizonEdge is called 3 times, and each call scans all faceCount faces (inner loop over fa/fb/fc). With up to MaxFaces=256 faces, that is ~3*F*F integer-compare iterations per EPA iteration, and up to 128 EPA iterations. This nested O(F^2) dominates EPA runtime and is pure pointer-chasing with poor vectorization.
perf.proposedChange: Compute the horizon by edge cancellation instead of repeated full scans. For each visible face, push its 3 directed edges into a small edge list; an edge that borders an invisible face survives, an edge shared by two visible faces cancels. Concretely: collect all directed edges of visible faces, then an edge (u,v) is a horizon edge iff its reverse (v,u) is NOT present among visible-face edges. Detect cancellation by sorting/scanning the visible edge list once (O(Ev log Ev) or O(Ev) with the existing horizonA/horizonB scratch used as a hash-free linear cancel buffer), rather than scanning ALL faces per edge. This removes the dependence on total faceCount and replaces it with dependence only on the (usually small) visible set.
perf.rationale: The visible face set is typically far smaller than faceCount; horizon edges number O(visible). Edge-cancellation touches each visible edge O(1) (amortized) instead of O(F). This drops the inner work from O(F^2) to ~O(Ev), a large asymptotic win on the hottest EPA loop, and the edge buffer is already allocated.
perf.risk: Must preserve winding/orientation so AddFace(horizonA[i], horizonB[i], newIdx) produces the same outward faces. Edge-cancel logic must treat (u,v) and (v,u) as the canceling pair exactly as IsHorizonEdge's 'shared edge with an invisible neighbor' rule does. Degenerate/duplicate vertices (collinear supports) could create non-manifold edges; keep the current AddFace len<Epsilon rejection so a spurious face is dropped. Validate against existing NUnit tests since this changes the horizon code path, not the math.

perf.summary: The 'visible' bool[MaxFaces] and horizon int[MaxFaces*EdgesPerFace] buffers are declared inside the EPA iteration loop; hoist their stackalloc to the method top to make frame usage explicit and avoid relying on JIT hoisting.
perf.currentCost: stackalloc bool[256] plus two stackalloc int[768] appear lexically inside the for(iter) body. C#/Burst hoists loop-invariant stackalloc to the frame, but expressing it in-loop obscures the ~6.5KB stack footprint and risks a stack-growth pattern if the JIT ever fails to hoist.
perf.proposedChange: Move 'bool* visible = stackalloc bool[MaxFaces];', 'int* horizonA = stackalloc int[MaxFaces*EdgesPerFace];', 'int* horizonB = ...' to the top of PenetrationDepth alongside the other stackalloc buffers, and just reset horizonCount=0 each iteration. The 'visible' array is fully overwritten each iteration so no clearing is needed.
perf.rationale: Guarantees single-allocation frame layout independent of optimizer behavior, keeps total stack budget visible for mobile, and removes any chance of repeated frame adjustment in the loop.
perf.risk: None semantically; buffers are fully written before read each iteration (visible[f] set for f<faceCount, horizonCount reset). Pure refactor.

perf.summary: AddFace computes math.length(n) (sqrt) for the degeneracy check AND to normalize; the degeneracy test can use lengthsq to avoid a sqrt on the reject path, and normalization can use rsqrt.
perf.currentCost: len = math.length(n) is a sqrt. It is used both as the degeneracy gate (len < Epsilon) and the normalizer (n = n/len). The compare-against-Epsilon does not need the true length, and n/len is a divide after a sqrt.
perf.proposedChange: Compute float lenSq = math.dot(n,n); reject when lenSq < Epsilon*Epsilon (use a named const EpsilonSq). Otherwise n = n * math.rsqrt(lenSq) to combine sqrt+divide into one reciprocal-sqrt multiply. Distance d still uses the normalized n via math.dot(n, vertices[a]).
perf.rationale: Removes one sqrt entirely on rejected/degenerate faces and converts the survivor path's sqrt+divide into rsqrt+multiply (fewer cycles, shorter dependency chain). AddFace runs per horizon edge per EPA iteration, so this is a hot leaf.
perf.risk: rsqrt is an approximation in some math libs but Unity.Mathematics math.rsqrt on float is accurate enough for normals here; if exact parity with math.length is required for test determinism, keep n = n * (1.0f / math.sqrt(lenSq)) which is bit-equivalent restructuring. The Epsilon^2 threshold differs from Epsilon for the length test: with Epsilon=1e-6, EpsilonSq=1e-12; a face with length between 1e-12 and 1e-6 would now pass instead of being rejected. To preserve EXACT behavior keep the gate as lenSq < EpsilonSq only if the intended threshold is on squared length; otherwise gate on math.length still. Recommend: reject when lenSq < Epsilon*Epsilon to keep the same true-length cutoff (sqrt(EpsilonSq)=Epsilon), which is exactly equivalent.

perf.summary: ExpandSimplex line-2 case calls math.length(ab) inside a comparison that can be squared to avoid a sqrt.
perf.currentCost: math.abs(ab.x) > DirectionThresholdRatio * math.length(ab) computes a sqrt to compare a magnitude against a scaled length. ExpandSimplex runs at most once per PenetrationDepth so impact is low, but the sqrt is avoidable.
perf.proposedChange: Compare squared quantities: ab.x*ab.x > (DirectionThresholdRatio*DirectionThresholdRatio) * math.lengthsq(ab), with a precomputed const for the squared ratio. Both sides are non-negative so the inequality is preserved.
perf.rationale: Removes a sqrt from the comparison; squaring both sides preserves ordering since both operands are >= 0.
perf.risk: math.abs(ab.x) and the RHS are both non-negative, so squaring preserves the comparison exactly. Floating-point rounding of the squared form differs by ULPs from the sqrt form at the exact threshold boundary, which could flip the perturbation-axis choice in a measure-zero case; result is still a valid expansion direction (this is heuristic seeding), so observable collision output is unaffected.
